text.p: The mark eased across the board here in the wake of the lira's return to the Europe's exchange rate mechanism on Monday after a four-year hiatus.

Analysts said that the lira's stronger-than-expected new ERM central rate at 990 per mark increased expectations of interest rate cuts in Italy and re-ignited interest in convergence plays in Italy and elsewhere in Europe. Italian government bond futures rallied further to test new record highs in early trade.
The firm lira ERM rate, which acted like a magnet in early trading here, helped lift the French franc too because it was seen to ease growing pressure on France's strong franc policy.

Prior to marathon talks on Saturday between senior European Union treasury and central bank officials and a meeting late Sunday of European finance ministers, the 990 central rate was seen as a compromise leaning more toward Franco-German demands than Italian government requests.

Analysts said the French and German delegations likely pushed heavily for a rate below 1,000 per mark, in order to prevent Italy locking into a rate which may prove uncompetitive for French and German exporters in the longer term.
At 1210 GMT, mark/lira was trading at 991.00/50 compared with 997.90/8.25 late Friday.

"The re-entry rate was slightly more demanding than the Italians had bargained for and is bound to lead to renewed appetite for convergence trades based on heightened interest rate cut hopes," said Michael Burke, economist at Citibank.

Burke said that the capital inflow associated with a renewed spate of demand for Italian bonds is likely to boost the currency over the next month or so as he expects to see a significant rate cut within the next couple of weeks.
In this scenario, the lira may well probe below 990, but a likely desire by the Bank of Italy to intervene to cap any sharp appreciation beyond the central rate will leave it orbiting 990.

Although the lira is officially allowed to fluctuate 15 percent either side of 990 - giving a massive range of between 852.59 and 1,149.56 - it is more likely the Italian authorities will informally target the old 2.25 percent narrow band from the 1979-to-1993 period.
A 2.25 percent band around 990 would give approximate rates of 968 to 1012 and shadowing this will be in step with central bank policy elsewhere in the ERM, especially France and Spain.
"The intense debate over the exact mid-rate shows there is belief among many finance ministers that central ERM rates will be the eventual fixings for EMU," said a trader at a U.S. bank.
The French franc reversed all last week's losses, meantime. At 1307 GMT, mark/French franc was trading at 3.3837/42 compared with 3.3908/12 late on Friday.
Analysts said there had been concerns a lira ERM rate weaker than 1,000 would increase pressure on the French government to heed recent internal calls to allow the franc to depreciate.

Instead, the lira rate was firm and weekend comments from French officials reinforced the committment to the existing franc fort policy. Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said mark/franc was fairly valued and government policy unchanged, while the junior coalition party UDF also voiced support for franc fort.

Bank of France board member Jean Boissonnat slammed comments last week from former French president Valery Giscard d'Estaing which called for franc depreciation against the mark. "Any devaluation means national impoverishment," he said. "It is only justified as a penalty for bad management."

Former French budget minister Nicolas Sarkozy, tipped by many to return to the cabinet in a new year reshuffle, also rallied round franc fort. "The consequences of (Giscard's appeal) were negative for the solidity of our currency and for the solidity of the Franco-German couple. That's not a good start." -- Mike Dolan, London newsroom +44 171 542 6762
